items.headline: Monti Fest: Where flowers, faith & 1st harvest meet
items.gist: As Mangalorean Catholics prepare for September 8, Monti Fest—the Feast of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary—brings together prayer, family, children, the harvest and a renewed call to care for creation. For nine days children carry colourful flowers to churches for the Flower Offering Novena; Monte Mariano at Farangipet near Mangaluru is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of the celebration.
items.paragraph: As Mangalorean Catholics prepare for September 8, Monti Fest—the Feast of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary—brings together prayer, family, children, the harvest and a renewed call to care for creation. For nine days children carry colourful flowers to churches for the Flower Offering Novena; Monte Mariano at Farangipet near Mangaluru is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of the celebration. The first corn of the season is blessed and shared, and Bishop Peter Paul Saldanha of Mangalore Diocese marks September 8 as Environment Day and Girl Child Day in the Diocese, urging respect for creation and water conservation in line with the Pope’s monthly intention.

items.headline: ‘Go Sanmaan Abhiyan’ to launch third phase
items.gist: The third phase of the ‘Go Sanmaan Abhiyan’ campaign to promote cow protection and conservation will be inaugurated at Sri Gorakshanatha Temple in Kadri, Mangaluru, on September 6 at 11 am in the presence of prominent seers. The campaign committee said a signature collection drive aims to mobilise public support and raise awareness about cattle’s importance in Indian culture, appealing to devotees and cow-protection supporters to participate; State coordinator Jeevan Ji, Dakshina Pranta Goseva Pramukh Praveen Saralaya, division dairy-products marketing chief Ashok Ilanthil and Mangaluru division Goseva Pramukh Gangadhar are among the organisers.

items.headline: Street vendors evicted in Hampankatta
items.gist: Mangaluru City Corporation officials launched an eviction drive on Thursday evening against street vendors who had illegally encroached footpaths in Hampankatta and surrounding areas, removing flowers and temporary structures and warning of stringent legal action against repeat encroachment. Dakshina Kannada Zilla Beedhibadhi Vyaparasthara Sangha Honorary President B K Imthiyaz condemned the drive, saying flower vendors from Hassan, Mandya and other districts had come for Krishnashtami and that the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 permits vending during festivals.

items.headline: ‘Police dept must make greater use of science, technology’
items.gist: Mangaluru Western Range Deputy Inspector General of Police Chetan R said the police department must make greater use of science and technology in maintaining law and order and detecting crimes, speaking at the valedictory of the 8th Mangaluru Western Range-level Police Duty Meet where he distributed prizes to competition winners. He stressed that dedicated performance by personnel from constables to senior officers was essential for a safe, peaceful society and the country’s progress.

items.headline: Case filed against associate NCC officers of NITK over financial irregularities
items.gist: Surathkal Police registered a case against NITK Associate NCC Officers Prof P Johnson and Prof H Shivananda after an internal Comptroller and Auditor General audit found TA/DA claim bills were based on false documents; the duo were detained and an internal investigation is underway. NITK Director B Ravi said the NCC unit must uphold morality and integrity, and appointed Dr Mohan Lal Meena, Assistant Professor in Chemical Engineering, as NCC caretaker officer in place of the ANOs.

items.headline: Sewing machines donated to Lady Goschen Hospital
items.gist: The Indian Red Cross Society, Dakshina Kannada District, donated three electric sewing machines to Government Lady Goschen Hospital on Thursday. Medical Superintendent Dr M R Durgaprasad said the machines will help restore surgical garments used by patients, doctors and nurses, and DK District IRCS Chairman Shantharam Shetty said the initiative would promote reuse of garments and indirectly strengthen government financial resources.

items.headline: Proposal for reconstruction of Karambar bridge
items.gist: The PWD sent a ₹2 crore reconstruction proposal in March 2025 after a portion of the 1963 arch bridge sank on Wednesday on the MIA–Bajpe SH-67. A temporary earthen culvert with concrete pipes allows light vehicles while heavy vehicles use alternate roads; city–airport traffic is unaffected as the bridge lies beyond MIA.

items.headline: New coconut milk residue-based food ingredient launched
items.gist: ICAR-CPCRI Kasaragod released Kalpa Composite Flour, mixing coconut milk residue with cereal and millet flours in three variants with a three-month shelf life and 10–25% CMR incorporation. Abhijnana Food Products in Puttur is commercializing Nitya brand millet and ragi cookies using the ingredient.

items.headline: Railways to install double boom barrier at Pandeshwar Level Crossing
items.gist: Palakkad Division, pending a road-over-bridge, will install a double boom-barrier at Pandeshwar Level Crossing at about ₹2 crore; tenders are open and work is expected to be finalised within a fortnight and completed in six months. MCC and the DC offered to widen a 200 m road stretch to four lanes when Railways widens the crossing; MLA Vedavyasa Kamath and MP Brijesh Chowta pursued the issue.

items.headline: Fraudster absconding for 14 years arrested
items.gist: The North sub-division crime detection team at Moodabidri has arrested Srinivasa B R (48) of Baithadka in Jallur village, Sullia taluk, who had absconded for 14 years without appearing before court in a fraud case involving lacs of rupees. Police said he availed a vehicle loan of Rs 10 lac from Shriram Finance in 2009 to purchase a Telcon EX 70 vehicle but failed to pay instalments or produce the vehicle for inspection; a case was registered at Moodabidri police station in 2012 and the court issued a non-bailable warrant in CC No 526/2025.

Police said he availed a vehicle loan of Rs 10 lac from Shriram Finance in 2009 to purchase a Telcon EX 70 vehicle but failed to pay instalments or produce the vehicle for inspection; a case was registered at Moodabidri police station in 2012 and the court issued a non-bailable warrant in CC No 526/2025. He was apprehended near Baithadka Junction on September 2 and produced before court; another warrant in a cheque bounce case is pending against him.

items.headline: Udupi cops arrest Cong leader, 2 others for extortion
items.gist: Kota Police have arrested Congress leader Nagendra Puthran (37) of Gobbarabettu in Kotathattu village, P Sumanth Kundar (40) of Padukere in Parampalli and Sachin Shriyan (32) of Sasthana for allegedly threatening to kill a man and demanding money over bags of rice kept in his front yard under the State government’s Anna Bhagya scheme. The complainant said the three verbally abused him and threatened extortion and murder on Monday, August 31; a team led by Sub-Inspectors Praveen Kumar R and Mahantesh Jabagouda under DSP Belliyappa KU and Brahmavara Circle Inspector Gopikrishna arrested Sachin on September 1 and the other two on September 2, and all three were produced before court.

items.headline: Udupi prepares for Krishna Janmashtami festivities
items.gist: Elaborate preparations are underway in Udupi for two-day Sri Krishna Janmashtami celebrations on September 4 and 5, with special pujas, a night arghya ceremony, a two-day tiger dance competition, and Vittlapindi on September 5 featuring traditional Mallayuddha at Shiruru Mutt and a golden chariot procession of a clay Krishna idol along Ratha Beedi. Organisers are preparing about 1.5 lakh chaklis and roughly 30,000 pieces each of five varieties of sweets using nearly 20 quintals of jaggery and seven quintals of sugar, with around 80 cooks involved; wrestlers from the Mysuru region have been invited, and Mutt Diwan Udayakumar Saralattaya said the mutt’s festival idol would not be taken out—instead a clay idol would be worshipped on September 4 and carried in procession the next day.

items.headline: Bhatkal ASP cracks down on sand trucks
items.gist: Bhatkal Sub-Divisional Assistant Superintendent of Police Ranu Gupta, IPS, has launched a crackdown on illegal sand transportation soon after taking charge, seizing six tipper trucks and detaining six persons—Harish, Ajit, Anand, Prakash, Maruti and Nazir. Police sources said three trucks were seized within Manki Police Station limits and three in Murdeshwar Police Station limits under ASP Ranu Gupta’s leadership, with cases registered at both stations and further investigation underway.

items.headline: International conference on Ayurveda from September 30
items.gist: Sri Dharmasthala Manjunatheshwara (SDM) College of Ayurveda, Hospital and Research Centre, Udupi, will organise KSHAMATVAM 2026, the sixth international conference on Translational Ayurveda In Autoimmune Disorders, from September 30 to October 1 at the Bhavaprakasha Auditorium, Udupi, with a pre-conference workshop on September 29. Under the theme ‘Translational Ayurveda in Autoimmune Disorders: Bridging Classical Wisdom with Global Healthcare’, the two-day programme will feature keynote lectures, scientific sessions, panel discussions, and paper and poster presentations, alongside an Ayurveda Expo showcasing pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, research and wellness services.

items.headline: Khader to launch Praja Seva Andolana in Puttur tomorrow
items.gist: Dakshina Kannada District In-charge Minister U T Khader will launch the ‘Praja Seva Andolana’, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar’s initiative to take government to people’s doorsteps, at the Town hall in Puttur on September 5. Praja Seva Abhiyan meetings will be held at taluk and hobli levels across the state every Saturday, with AI-based outbound calls and Gram One kiosks at venues; grievances will be handled through separate new and unresolved queues, and eligible beneficiaries will receive on-the-spot sanction letters at meetings.

items.headline: Banks told to ensure timely, adequate credit for eligible farmers
items.gist: Udupi Zilla Panchayat CEO Prateek Bayal told a district-level Lead Bank progress review meeting that banks must ensure eligible farmers receive timely and adequate credit, adopt a friendly approach to beneficiaries, and strengthen awareness on preventing financial fraud, including use of 1600-series numbers for transaction calls. As of June-end the district had 440 bank branches with deposits of Rs 48,715.93 crore and advances of Rs 24,184.84 crore, a credit-deposit ratio of 49.64% against the RBI minimum of 60%, and annual credit plan achievement of 39.41% (Rs 7,302.87 crore of Rs 18,532.26 crore).

items.headline: Forest staff seek divine intervention to tackle elephant menace
items.gist: Belthangady forest department staff offered ‘Rangapooja’ at the Sowthadka Shree Mahaganapathi kshetra in Kokkada, praying that wild elephants would not cause loss of human life or damage to agriculture. During 2026-27, over 80 wild elephants destroyed crops and areca plantations worth over Rs 77 lakh in Belthangady, Sullia and Kadaba taluks; Rs 3.30 lakh compensation was released to 19 people while Rs 73 lakh remained pending for 381, and forest officials have submitted a proposal to establish an elephant camp at Gundya.

items.headline: K'taka govt blinks; Parks Bill 'buried in the tunnel'
items.gist: The Karnataka government has decided to withdraw the controversial amendment to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, which allowed a 5% diversion of park land for public utility use. Briefing reporters after a cabinet meeting on Thursday, September 3, Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said the Bill would be withdrawn, placed in the public domain for discussion, and reintroduced in the next session with amendments; the government will also inform the Governor.
items.paragraph: The Karnataka government has decided to withdraw the controversial amendment to the Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) Act, which allowed a 5% diversion of park land for public utility use. Briefing reporters after a cabinet meeting on Thursday, September 3, Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said the Bill would be withdrawn, placed in the public domain for discussion, and reintroduced in the next session with amendments; the government will also inform the Governor. The announcement came two days after Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said they would revisit the amendment amid massive public protests, notably in Lalbagh, where several acres could be diverted for the CM's tunnel road project if the amendment stood.

items.headline: K'taka targets 66 GW power capacity by 2030, puts clean energy at core
items.gist: Karnataka has unveiled a 10-year roadmap to raise its installed power capacity from over 39 GW currently to 66 GW by 2030, with the expansion expected to be overwhelmingly focused on clean energy, the Energy Department said on Thursday. Additional Chief Secretary, Energy Department, Gaurav Gupta outlined the roadmap at the Focus State Session for Karnataka during Bharat Electricity, POWER-GEN India and Indian Utility Week 2026 at Yashobhoomi in Bengaluru.
items.paragraph: Karnataka has unveiled a 10-year roadmap to raise its installed power capacity from over 39 GW currently to 66 GW by 2030, with the expansion expected to be overwhelmingly focused on clean energy, the Energy Department said on Thursday. Additional Chief Secretary, Energy Department, Gaurav Gupta outlined the roadmap at the Focus State Session for Karnataka during Bharat Electricity, POWER-GEN India and Indian Utility Week 2026 at Yashobhoomi in Bengaluru. Electricity demand is expected to double over the next decade, and Karnataka expects to attract Rs two lakh crore to Rs three lakh crore in private investment in the power sector over the next four to five years while advancing projects including the 2,000 MW Sharavathi Pumped Storage Project and expansion of the Pavagada Solar Park.

items.headline: Wipro to invest Rs 1k cr in hydraulic pump manufacturing plant
items.gist: Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery, a manufacturer of hydraulic pumps, has come forward to establish a manufacturing plant with an investment of Rs 1,000 crore in Karnataka, state Large and Medium Industries Minister M B Patil said on Thursday. The project, proposed to be set up in Phase V of the Harohalli Industrial Area, is expected to generate employment for around 1,200 people.

items.headline: KAT stays suspension of two teachers over RSS march participation
items.gist: The Kalaburagi bench of the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal has stayed the suspension of government primary school teachers Gururaj Joshi of Hunasagi town and Anna Saheb Deshmukh of Kuppi school in Yadgir district, who were accused of participating in an RSS route march in Hunasagi on October 10, 2025, wearing the organisation’s uniform. Deputy Director Channabasappa Madhol had suspended them on August 20 following a government direction after complaints, including from Ambedkar Swabhimani Sena district president Jummanna Gudimani to ministers Priyank Kharge and Madhu Bangarappa; the teachers said the Sunday event was cultural and outside working hours, but the department held it a prima facie violation of Karnataka Civil Services (Conduct) Rules.

items.headline: BSNL SIM cards for 67 rural post offices
items.gist: Financial and postal services in 67 rural post offices across Karnataka have been restored following intervention by Uttara Kannada MP Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri over a non-availability of BSNL SIM cards that had blocked India Post Payments Bank and other digital services for senior citizens, farmers, widows and persons with disabilities relying on postal banking. Of the affected offices, 43 were in Uttara Kannada, 22 in Shivamogga and two in Chikkamagaluru district; these locations had no private telecom network apart from BSNL, making the SIM shortage a major hurdle for pension and welfare transactions.

items.headline: Kodavas reiterate demand for special constitutional status
items.gist: The Codava National Council reiterated its demand for special constitutional status and greater political autonomy for the Codava community at its 31st annual public Kailpoud celebrations at Capitol Village, Madikeri, on September 1. CNC president N.U.
items.paragraph: The Codava National Council reiterated its demand for special constitutional status and greater political autonomy for the Codava community at its 31st annual public Kailpoud celebrations at Capitol Village, Madikeri, on September 1. CNC president N.U. Nachappa said the organisation would continue efforts for constitutional recognition and listed 10 demands including geopolitical autonomy for Codavaland, special ethnic classification, inclusion of Codava Thakk in the Eighth Schedule, protection of the traditional gun, UNESCO recognition of Codava heritage, an Inner Line Permit system, a separate legislative constituency and restoration of hereditary lands; Federation of New States vice-president Mettaramarao (IRS, VRS) said the Codavaland demand was among the oldest statehood claims and deserved priority.

items.headline: Min meets CWC chairman, seeks technical clearance for Mekedatu project
items.gist: Water Resources Minister N Chaluvarayaswamy held a high-level meeting with Central Water Commission Chairman Anupam Prasad in New Delhi on Wednesday to seek statutory and technical approvals for the Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir Project across the Cauvery river. items.headline: Bail plea of MLA's daughter dismissed

items.headline: Fix sugarcane price, install fencing for farmers: AAP
items.gist: Aam Aadmi Party leaders staged a protest from Ambedkar Circle in Bidar to the Deputy Commissioner's office and submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister through the DC, urging the government to fix sugarcane prices for district farmers at ₹4,000 to ₹4,500 per tonne and install fencing around farmers' fields to protect crops from wild animals entering from nearby forest areas. The leaders cited rising production costs, noted that sugarcane farmers in Punjab are paid ₹4,160 per tonne, and demanded a special scheme to protect Bidar farmers facing significant crop losses from frequent wild-animal incursions.

items.headline: Jeweller's house burgled in Tumakuru, valuables worth Rs 2.25 crore stolen
items.gist: Gold and silver ornaments and other valuables worth around Rs 2.25 crore were stolen from jeweller Laksham Ganpat Pawar's house in Tumakuru when he and his family were away in Sangli, Maharashtra for his son's wedding on August 29 and 30, police said on Thursday. Thieves broke in after cutting the grill on the compound wall and windows, wore masks to avoid identification, and stole gold biscuits, silver bars, and silver coins.

items.headline: BJP's 'Ballari Chalo' padayatra enters Sindhanur; Vijayendra raises farmers' issues
items.gist: The third day of the BJP's 'Ballari Chalo' padayatra, organised to highlight alleged administrative failures of the Congress government and problems faced by farmers and oppressed communities, concluded in Sindhanur on Thursday after covering about 20 km from Gudadoor. BJP state president B Y Vijayendra, who led the march from a bullock cart carrying a plough, demanded crop loans of drought-hit farmers be waived up to Rs 5 lakh, alleged diversion of Scheduled Caste and Tribal Sub-Plan funds, claimed 3,655 farmer suicides in Karnataka over the past three years including 937 in Kalyana Karnataka, and welcomed the government's decision to hold a special legislature session from September 21 to 23 while saying the BJP would raise issues including agricultural loan waiver during proceedings.

items.paragraph: One year after the Greater Bengaluru Authority became operational on 2 September last year, splitting the erstwhile BBMP into five smaller corporations, public infrastructure experts say Bengaluru still has no elected council since September 2020 and its civic problems have compounded. items.headline: Rain deficit drives rise in crop insurance enrolment
items.gist: A severe monsoon deficit across Karnataka has driven a record surge in farmer enrolment for the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, with kharif registrations nearly doubling from 20,91,575 in 2025 to 37,45,804 in 2026 as the last date for enrolment ended on August 31. Economically backward and drought-prone districts of Kalaburagi, Bidar, Haveri, Vijayapura, Gadag and Chitradurga account for half of total farmers who insured kharif crops, with around 23% coming from the tur-growing belt of Kalaburagi and Bidar.
items.paragraph: A severe monsoon deficit across Karnataka has driven a record surge in farmer enrolment for the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, with kharif registrations nearly doubling from 20,91,575 in 2025 to 37,45,804 in 2026 as the last date for enrolment ended on August 31. Economically backward and drought-prone districts of Kalaburagi, Bidar, Haveri, Vijayapura, Gadag and Chitradurga account for half of total farmers who insured kharif crops, with around 23% coming from the tur-growing belt of Kalaburagi and Bidar. Farmer leaders including Karnataka Prantha Raitha Sangha's Kalaburagi district president Sharanabasappa Mamashetty criticised the compensation formula and random yield assessment, noting the government and insurance companies have not yet disbursed 20% of the previous year's crop insurance compensation; Agriculture Department Director Dr G T Putra said the last kharif installment has been released and rabi processing initiated, citing awareness campaigns after rainfall deficit forecasts that yielded a record 49.5 lakh agriculture and horticulture farmer applications under Fasal Bima Yojana.

items.headline: KIA plans home check-in, courier service
items.gist: Kempegowda International Airport is planning home check-in, courier and personal shopper services, with airport official Lewis saying passengers could send items left behind at security to their destination via a tracking mechanism and that courier and personal shopper services are likely in coming months while home check-in needs more time for legal requirements. Care by BLR currently offers meet-and-assist, baggage storage, porter assistance, valet parking, lounges and chauffeur-driven transport priced roughly between Rs 500 and Rs 7,000, with limousine services starting around Rs 4,500–Rs 5,000 and Rolls-Royce service about Rs 50,000 and above; about 24 kiosks operate across both terminals and the airport is considering extending services outside Bengaluru through tie-ups.

items.headline: State okays dept on overseas affairs, global investments
items.gist: The Cabinet approved a department on overseas affairs and global investments hoped to foster global sister-city partnerships in mobility, urban governance, innovation, culture, museum and trade while connecting with global institutions for health, medicine and leisure tourism. A state facilitation council headed by the chief minister with the deputy CM as vice-chairman and 11 ministers will promote cross-sector linkages; for the first time a 10-member Group of Ministers headed by the CM—including G Parameshwara, K H Muniyappa, K J George, Priyank Kharge, Krishna Byre Gowda, Dr Yathindra Siddaramaiah, U T Khader, Laxman Savadi, Satish Jarkiholi and M B Patil—will scrutinise important policy decisions before Cabinet, and the Cabinet approved eight government spokespersons who will receive a daily morning briefing on important decisions and the official stand.

items.headline: Bengaluru housing boom leaves Rs 40-lakh...
items.gist: Developers and analysts said Bengaluru's affordable housing benchmark needs updating as a Rs 40–45 lakh home in 2016 would cost roughly Rs 79–89 lakh today at 7% annual inflation, with soaring land and construction costs pushing developers toward properties priced at Rs 1.5 crore and above where average selling prices are close to Rs 10,000 per sq ft in most micro-markets. The share of Rs 40 lakh–Rs 80 lakh homes fell from 57% of sales in 2022 to 30% in 2023, 24% in 2024 and 7% in 2025 before marginally recovering to 8% in H1 2026, while the Rs 80 lakh–Rs 1.5 crore segment accounted for 30% in H1 2026; annual sales rose from 49,480 units in 2022 to 74,260 in 2025 with 31,720 in H1 2026, even as withdrawal of developer tax incentives under 80-IBA reduced cushion for affordable projects and achievable realisations below Rs 40 lakh are broadly limited to around Rs 4,000–Rs 4,200 per sq ft.

items.headline: As Modi plans for 2047, Karnataka sets targets for 2037
items.gist: While broadly aligning with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, Congress-governed Karnataka has set 2037 as its deadline for goals including poverty eradication, with Chief Minister D K Shivakumar's Finance Advisor L K Atheeq saying the state will focus on Karnataka @ 2037 and interim targets for 2032—the next six years—in a consultative exercise also covering 2047. On Wednesday, NITI Aayog vice-chairperson Ashok Kumar Lahiri gave Shivakumar a presentation on envisioning 2047; the think tank flagged four macro challenges—regional imbalance beyond Bengaluru, a rural-urban per-capita income divide, unplanned urbanisation and climate resilience—and said Karnataka's strengths lie in IT, global capability centres, startups, aerospace, electronics and biotechnology.

items.headline: Gen Z emerges as 'fifth estate' in Bengaluru youth dialogue
items.gist: The growing political awareness of Gen Z and its role in shaping India's democratic discourse came into focus at The GenZ Reckoning, a Salmaan Ahmed initiative in Bengaluru on Thursday that let young participants question political leaders on education, careers, leadership, culture, urban development and the future. The dialogue featured N A Haris, Dinesh Gundu Rao, Dr C N Ashwath Narayan, Ramya, Pawan Khera, Rizwan Arshad, Revathi Kamath, S R Vishwanath and Mohammed Haris Nalapad; Rao rejected the perception that young people lack political awareness and described citizen movements, youth-led NGOs and public participation as an emerging "fifth estate" that can address shortcomings in traditional democratic institutions, while cautioning against misinformation through unregulated social media echo chambers and calling for scientific temper.

items.headline: KPSC scam: CID conducts mahazar at suspect's Bengaluru house
items.gist: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) on Thursday conducted a spot mahazar at the Sanjay Nagar, Bengaluru residential premises of Basavaraj Kannale, one of two key suspects in custody in the alleged Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) irregularities. Kannale, described as the linchpin of the scam, allegedly orchestrated irregularities from Bengaluru and Bhalki, Bidar, with deals with candidates suspected to have been executed at the Sanjay Nagar house; the CID had previously searched it before his arrest.

items.headline: Protest against river linking projects gathers momentum in U-K
items.gist: The Bedti-Varada and Aghanashini-Vedavati river linking projects have drawn intense opposition from local communities and environmentalists, with Save Gangavali-Karavali awareness campaigns under the Bedti-Aghanashini basin conservation committee held at Gokarna, Karwar and Ankola on Thursday. More than 10,000 letters to Chief Minister demanding the projects be dropped were submitted to Deputy Commissioner K Lakshmipriya; committee president Ananth Hegde Ashishara said expert reports show low water flow in Bedti and Aghanashini rivers and warned the projects could adversely impact Kadamba Naval Base.

More than 10,000 letters to Chief Minister demanding the projects be dropped were submitted to Deputy Commissioner K Lakshmipriya; committee president Ananth Hegde Ashishara said expert reports show low water flow in Bedti and Aghanashini rivers and warned the projects could adversely impact Kadamba Naval Base. Former minister Anand Asnotikar, BJP state vice-president Rupali Naik and others attended as Gokarna saw a protest march; the Bedti-Varada project proposes diverting surplus west-flowing Bedti water to the east-flowing Varada to supply drinking water to arid districts including Haveri.

items.headline: B'luru economy at $400 bn by 2037: Five growth drivers identified
items.gist: An Economic Master Plan draft presented to Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Wednesday aims to transform the Bengaluru Metropolitan Region (BMR) into a $400-billion economy by 2037, when Bengaluru marks 500 years as a city, with 2–2.5 million jobs envisaged under a plan prepared with ISEG Foundation as knowledge partner. Five growth drivers are identified: technology, next-generation manufacturing, healthcare and education, infrastructure and sustainability, and planned urbanisation; IT, GCCs, AI and startups are flagged as biggest contributors, with proposals including dedicated IT/GCC hubs, deep-tech sandboxes, a dedicated AI mission, raising public transport modal share from 35% to 75% via Metro, suburban rail and RRTS, a second airport, ring/radial/chord roads, water augmentation and reuse, planned cities, affordable housing and slum rehabilitation.

Five growth drivers are identified: technology, next-generation manufacturing, healthcare and education, infrastructure and sustainability, and planned urbanisation; IT, GCCs, AI and startups are flagged as biggest contributors, with proposals including dedicated IT/GCC hubs, deep-tech sandboxes, a dedicated AI mission, raising public transport modal share from 35% to 75% via Metro, suburban rail and RRTS, a second airport, ring/radial/chord roads, water augmentation and reuse, planned cities, affordable housing and slum rehabilitation. The BMR is currently a $149-billion economy across three districts, with per capita income nearly twice the state average.

items.headline: HC notice to ECI on appointing anganwadi workers as BLOs
items.gist: The High Court of Karnataka on Thursday ordered notice to the Election Commission of India (ECI), the Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka and the state government in a PIL by the Karnataka State Anganwadi Workers and Helpers Union, State Committee, Davangere, against appointing anganwadi workers as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls unless non-availability of eligible regular state or local government employees is recorded. A division bench of Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K S Hemalekha posted the matter to December 1; the petitioners cited ECI guidelines dated June 5, 2025 requiring BLOs first from Group C and above regular employees, with anganwadi workers only as a fallback subject to Non-Availability Certificate compliance, and sought review and substitution of existing anganwadi BLO deployments while stressing the PIL does not seek to obstruct elections.

items.headline: Cabinet decides to withdraw contentious Parks Bill
items.gist: The Cabinet on Thursday decided to withdraw the contentious Parks bill (Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Act, 2026) by means of an ordinance, following backlash from citizens and Opposition parties. The bill, passed in the monsoon session, had amended the 1975 Act governing Bengaluru's lung spaces including Cubbon Park and Lalbagh to allow 5% park land for public purpose; Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said it would be reintroduced in the next full-fledged session after modifications based on suggestions, with contentious clauses related to sale, lease, gift and mortgage to be reviewed after public consultations.
items.paragraph: The Cabinet on Thursday decided to withdraw the contentious Parks bill (Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Act, 2026) by means of an ordinance, following backlash from citizens and Opposition parties. The bill, passed in the monsoon session, had amended the 1975 Act governing Bengaluru's lung spaces including Cubbon Park and Lalbagh to allow 5% park land for public purpose; Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said it would be reintroduced in the next full-fledged session after modifications based on suggestions, with contentious clauses related to sale, lease, gift and mortgage to be reviewed after public consultations. The Cabinet withdrew the bill after discussing acquisition of land in Lalbagh, Bengaluru Palace and Cubbon Park for the tunnel road project; Chief Minister D K Shivakumar posted on X that the decision reflected the government's commitment to respect public opinion and reintroduce the Bill with necessary amendments.

items.headline: State BJP chief demands farm loan waiver up to Rs 5L
items.gist: Karnataka BJP president B Y Vijayendra has urged the state government to waive crop loans up to Rs 5 lakh, addressing a press conference after concluding the third day of the 'Ballari Chalo' padayatra in Sindhanur on Thursday. He demanded a special legislature session to discuss farmers' problems due to rainfall deficit, said the BJP government under B S Yediyurappa had released Rs 14 crore for the Navali balancing reservoir to address 30 tmcft silt accumulation in Tungabhadra reservoir while the current government had taken no measures, and cited 3,655 farmer suicides since Congress came to power—including 936 in Kalyana Karnataka in three years, with 294 in Kalaburagi, 220 in Bidar, 160 in Raichur and more than 80 in Koppal—and pending dues of Rs 145 crore to farmers for white jowar procurement.

items.headline: Cabinet panel discusses UPSC model to end KPSC woes
items.gist: The first meeting of the Cabinet sub-committee on student issues and exam reforms was held on Thursday, deciding to collect opinions from experts including former vice chancellors before meeting stakeholders including students and parents. School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa suggested proper publicity and a separate website for public suggestions; Medical Education Minister Dr Sharanprakash Patil said no decision was taken at the first meeting and members also deliberated on the KPSC issue, with some suggesting adoption of the Union Public Service Commission model and senior ministers expressing displeasure over KPSC's failure to conduct fair exams.
items.paragraph: The first meeting of the Cabinet sub-committee on student issues and exam reforms was held on Thursday, deciding to collect opinions from experts including former vice chancellors before meeting stakeholders including students and parents. School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa suggested proper publicity and a separate website for public suggestions; Medical Education Minister Dr Sharanprakash Patil said no decision was taken at the first meeting and members also deliberated on the KPSC issue, with some suggesting adoption of the Union Public Service Commission model and senior ministers expressing displeasure over KPSC's failure to conduct fair exams. The committee is headed by Health Minister U T Khader with Home Minister Priyank Kharge and Higher Education Minister Basavaraj Rayareddi as members, and has one month's time to submit its report after wider consultations.

items.headline: Special session from Sep 21-23
items.gist: A special session of the legislature will be convened from September 21 to 23 exclusively to discuss the deepening agrarian crisis and the Dr Kasturirangan report on the Western Ghats. Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said this year is seeing the severest drought in 150 years due to super El Nino, impacting farmers, the state's economy and food security, that there was no opportunity to discuss this in the last session, and that although the government has rejected the Kasturirangan report many times it is coming up for discussion frequently and the government wants to discuss it in detail.

items.headline: First Nagendra, now Parks Bill: BJP claims two victories
items.gist: Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka on Thursday termed the Karnataka Cabinet's decision to withdraw the Bill allowing 5% of park land to be used for infrastructure projects a victory for the BJP's 'Save Parks, Save Bengaluru' campaign. Ashoka said the BJP recorded two victories in a month—last week Bellary MLA B Nagendra resigned from Shivakumar's Cabinet over the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki ST Development Corporation scam following BJP agitation—and charged the Bill would have been disastrous for future generations, that the 1975 Government Parks (Preservation) Act was meant to preserve green cover while flooding has increased in areas such as HSR Layout, Jayanagar and Hebbal, and that the government wanted to destroy parks to facilitate a tunnel road project for industrialist Gautam Adani; he said the BJP would oppose any future attempt to divert park land and had been preparing protests targeting five lakh signatures.

items.headline: Cabinet clears sites for 1,453 BMIC land losers in Bidadi: DCM
items.gist: The Karnataka cabinet on Thursday decided to allot sites to 1,453 farmers who parted with their land for the Bengaluru-Mysore Infrastructure Corridor (BMIC) project in the Bidadi sector, Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said after the Cabinet sub-committee on BMIC held eight meetings. Issues relating to site distribution in Sector-A Bidadi have been mostly resolved while toll collection, townships, intersection and link road will be tackled in phases; with only 574 sites available (231 of 30x40 and 243 of 40x60) for 1,453 land losers, another 879 sites will be created across Varahasandra, Madavara, Kodigenahalli and Srikantapura Linganandanahalli with NICE providing land within two months, and the government on humanitarian consideration decided to give all sites even if not mentioned in the agreement following the Supreme Court's direction that the state could decide in Cabinet.

items.headline: Shikhar, Mohsin script stunning recovery for Prez XI
items.gist: Tail-enders Shikhar Shetty (92 off 143 balls) and Mohsin Khan (51 not out off 50) forged a 101-run unbroken tenth-wicket stand as KSCA President's XI rallied from 295/9 to 396 all out to take the first-innings lead against Goa in the Dr (Capt) K Thimmappiah Memorial tournament at M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Thursday, leaving Goa reeling at 167/8 at stumps. At SDNRW Ground, Mysuru, KSCA Combined XI lost by an innings and 18 runs to Jharkhand after being bowled out for 66 and 273.

items.headline: Karnataka's Sindhushree, Supriya in Asian Games squad
items.gist: Women's pole vault national record holder Sindhushree G and high jumper Supriya B are among six Karnataka track and field athletes in the 77-member Indian squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya from September 19 to October 4, with Supriya having cleared 1.80m at the National Inter-State Championships and won gold at the World Athletics Continental Tour Silver Meet in Bhubaneswar. Neeraj Chopra was replaced by Yashvir Singh after pulling out with an ankle ligament tear, while Abhishek Pal was omitted after a prohibited substance was found in his dope sample.

items.headline: KBA to host 3 big events beginning with South Zone meet from tomorrow
items.gist: The Karnataka Badminton Association will host three major tournaments, starting with the 80th South Zone Inter-State Badminton Championship in Bengaluru from September 5 to 8 — the event's return to the city after 23 years — followed by the inaugural KBA Diamond Jubilee India International Challenge from October 27 to November 1 with USD 25,000 prize money and the Junior Nationals in early December. Former national champion Raghu M and women's doubles pair Ashwini Bhat and Shikha Gautam will spearhead Karnataka's 34-member squad.

items.headline: Nupura makes record sprint
items.gist: Karnataka's 100m hurdler Nupura Holla clocked 13.78 seconds to win gold and break the 14-year-old meet record of 14.06 at the National Youth Athletics Championships in Ludhiana on Thursday, coming close to the U-18 national record of 13.70. Karnataka finished third on the medals tally with three gold and two silver, and javelin thrower Pushpak Nelwade took silver with 76.09m.

items.headline: Eviction fear grips many Bengal migrant workers in Bengaluru
items.gist: Operation Mukta, aimed at identifying and tracking illegal immigrants in Bengaluru, has left nearly 400 migrant workers from West Bengal in and around Hulimangala in Electronics City anxious after police served show-cause notices on landlords of premises allegedly used for unauthorised garbage segregation citing health and sanitation concerns. Workers who have lived in the city for years as garbage segregators said they were not involved in any illegal activity and appealed to authorities to distinguish between illegal immigrants and genuine migrant labourers.

items.headline: SC: Bar council can't punish law students
items.gist: The Supreme Court ruled Thursday that the Bar Council of India and state bar councils lack statutory authority to take disciplinary action against law students, holding such powers arise only after enrolment as advocates. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified disciplinary control over students rests solely with their parent institutions or authorities under institutional regulations and byelaws.
items.paragraph: The Supreme Court ruled Thursday that the Bar Council of India and state bar councils lack statutory authority to take disciplinary action against law students, holding such powers arise only after enrolment as advocates. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified disciplinary control over students rests solely with their parent institutions or authorities under institutional regulations and byelaws. The court was hearing a writ petition by NALSAR alumni Mihira Sood and Abhishek Tiwari challenging BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra's August 13 directions to bar NALSAR's 2026 graduating batch from enrolment and order an inquiry over a campaign against the CJI; the BCI later withdrew those directions after public backlash. The bench declared the August 13 communications and any subsequent modified versions were "without any authority of law," made absolute its earlier order protecting NALSAR students and faculty from punitive action by the BCI or state bar councils, and disposed of the petition.

items.headline: 'Let's both show our degrees': Abhijeet Dipke challenges PM
items.gist: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to make their educational degrees public, reigniting controversy over Dipke's educational credentials at Boston University. In a post on X, Dipke said he was willing to show his degree from the US university if Prime Minister Modi agreed to disclose his qualifications.
items.paragraph: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke has challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to make their educational degrees public, reigniting controversy over Dipke's educational credentials at Boston University. In a post on X, Dipke said he was willing to show his degree from the US university if Prime Minister Modi agreed to disclose his qualifications. The issue resurfaced after a recent podcast hosted by Prakhar Gupta, in conversation with Sonam Wangchuk, included a clip discussing a friend who studied at Boston University and had participated in protests associated with Dipke's CJP.

items.headline: Hyderabad: Detonators seized, case booked
items.gist: As many as 160 detonators were found abandoned in a private real estate venture in the Secunderabad Cantonment on September 2, under Bolarum police limits, during intensified checks after assault rifles, pistols, magazines and ammunition were stolen from an Army facility on August 31. A senior police official said the recovery is not linked to the Army theft and that the detonators are suspected to have been used by land developers more than a year ago to explode boulders.

items.headline: Protester at Jarange's Maratha quota stir dies
items.gist: Dashrath Raikar, a resident of Sangam about 100 km from Jalna, died on Thursday of a suspected heart attack after travelling to Antarwali Sarati village to support activist Manoj Jarange's six-day hunger strike for Maratha reservation. Fellow protesters found him unresponsive on Thursday morning after he slept in a parking area near the protest site Wednesday night; doctors at a government hospital in Ambad declared him dead, and his body was sent for post-mortem to confirm the cause.

items.headline: Andhra Pradesh ACB arrests TTD top officer for graft
items.gist: Andhra Pradesh Anti-Corruption Bureau officials on Thursday arrested Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams Deputy Executive Officer B Lokanatham on corruption charges after raids at his residence and office that began on Wednesday morning. ACB teams seized documents pertaining to properties worth Rs 5 crore, along with 2 kg of gold, 6.5 kg of silver and Rs 12 lakh in cash, following a tip-off that he possessed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income.

items.headline: Two rescued from bonded labour
items.gist: Two persons were rescued from alleged bonded labour in a raid at a cowshed in Wadvani tehsil, Beed district, after legal aid volunteers flagged the matter to Collector Vivek Johnson and DLSA chairman Dinesh P Surana ordered an immediate rescue. The two were allegedly kept captive, assaulted and forced to work up to 15 hours a day for two months; five other workers remain missing after the owner allegedly moved them under cover of darkness, and Tehsildar Vaibhav Mahendrakar was bitten by a dog during the September 1 raid amid power cuts and no mobile connectivity.

items.headline: Ram Temple 'corporatisation' has started, says Raut
items.gist: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said on Thursday that appointing retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as the first CEO of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, alongside a major overhaul after donation-theft allegations, means the Ayodhya temple's "corporatisation" has begun. Raut also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's praise of 7.8 per cent GDP growth, citing former finance secretary Subhash Garg's claim that growth would have been about 2.6 per cent in current prices without last year's GDP revision down from roughly Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore, and asked why the government still gives free food grains to 85 crore citizens and Rs 1500 under Ladki Bahin.

items.headline: Social media influencer arrested for 'objectionable' remarks against Maha Min
items.gist: Pune police arrested 45-year-old social media influencer Santosh Pandit from his residence on Thursday for allegedly posting obscene, sexually suggestive and defamatory YouTube content against Maharashtra Higher and Technical Education Minister Chandrakant Patil and a public representative, with objectionable remarks about Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis in another video. Kothrud police registered the case at 1:30 am under BNS sections 75(1)(iv), 75(3), 356(2) and 352 and Section 67 of the IT Act; DCP Sagar Kawade confirmed the arrest, and this is Pandit's second Pune case over remarks against Patil after an earlier complaint at Deccan police station.

items.headline: Edu is a right, marginalised students must not face neglect: Rahul Gandhi
items.gist: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said during his Wednesday visit to Nashik that education is not a privilege but the right of every student in India, and students from marginalised communities should not face neglect from the system. He met a delegation of tribal students, including some on hunger strike over issues including the condition of ashram schools meant for tribals, listened to their problems, and asserted that every student deserves a respectful, safe and conducive study environment with full system support.

items.headline: Goa to provide 3 free LPG cylinders to citizens annually
items.gist: Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant announced on Thursday that the state will provide three LPG cylinders free of cost annually by crediting Rs 3,000 every year into beneficiaries' bank accounts from September 9, fulfilling a 2022 assembly election promise. Forms will be available at panchayats and with MLAs from September 5; beneficiaries must submit copies of bank passbook, Aadhaar card and voter identity card to receive the assistance toward three cylinders.

items.headline: Activist seeking ban on music ahead of Ganesh festival assaulted in Pune
items.gist: City-based activist Vidyanand Bapat, who has vocally opposed high-decibel DJ systems and loudspeakers before Ganeshotsav, was slapped by Santosh Chavan while speaking to electronic media on Tilak Road around 11 am Thursday; the assault was captured on camera and police escorted Bapat away. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the attacker was arrested and assaulting anyone for voicing views was wrong, while Pune Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar pledged strict action; Bapat had shot to prominence last month when Ganesh mandal representatives became aggressive after he sought a ban on amplified DJ music at a Pune Municipal Corporation meeting ahead of the September 14 festival.

items.headline: Telangana CM sacks Forest Minister Konda Surekha
items.gist: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy decided on Thursday to drop Forest and Endowments Minister Konda Surekha from the Council of Ministers with immediate effect and recommended the move to Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla, amid a row over critical remarks by her daughter against the chief minister and other party leaders. He also rescinded G Chinna Reddy's appointment as Vice Chairman of the State Planning Board and appointed Women's Commission Chairperson Gadwal Vijayalakshmi as the new VC, following confabulations with AICC leaders in Delhi after the state Congress disciplinary committee recommended tough action against Surekha and Chinna Reddy.

items.headline: Oppn slams BJP as Nabin welcomes Russian envoy with 'Rasputin' playing in background
items.gist: When BJP chief Nitin Nabin met Russian envoy Denis Alipov at party headquarters on Tuesday, he shared a video of the meeting with Boney M’s 1978 hit “Ra Ra Rasputin” playing in the background, drawing criticism from Congress and Trinamool leaders including Abhishek Manu Singhvi, Supriya Shrinate, Mahua Moitra, and Saket Gokhale, who called it comical, tasteless, and insulting to Russia because the song is widely used in memes about Vladimir Putin. Nabin said the meeting was warm and productive, covering India-Russia ties and the BJP’s history and organisation, and the BJP is yet to comment on the opposition criticism.

items.headline: Aid to schools in WB to be cut if Vande Mataram is not sung in
items.gist: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari warned on Thursday that financial aid and other government support to schools would be stopped if the mandatory singing of the full version of Vande Mataram during school prayers was not strictly followed. Addressing an RSS-affiliated organisation in Kolkata, he said the BJP dispensation was undertaking reforms to restore Indian culture and nationalist values in school education, and claimed scholarships from classes 5–8 under the previous TMC government were made available only to Muslim students.
items.paragraph: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari warned on Thursday that financial aid and other government support to schools would be stopped if the mandatory singing of the full version of Vande Mataram during school prayers was not strictly followed. He also said he had written to Defence Minister Rajnath Singh seeking permission to make NCC mandatory in schools and colleges.

items.headline: Satheesan's FB post against Islamic scholar missing
items.gist: A post by Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan criticising senior Islamic scholar Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar over alleged anti-women remarks has gone missing from his Facebook page, though it remains on Instagram, the CMO said on Thursday attributing the disappearance to a technical error from linking between the platforms. The post contained a portion of video from his Wednesday press conference; the CMO rejected reports that it was removed after protests by Sunni Muslim leaders who met Satheesan at the CMO.

what_this_is.purpose: The post contained a portion of video from his Wednesday press conference; the CMO rejected reports that it was removed after protests by Sunni Muslim leaders who met Satheesan at the CMO.

items.headline: ED raids in Keralam in drug smuggling case
items.gist: The Enforcement Directorate conducted raids at multiple locations across Kerala on Thursday in a money-laundering probe linked to two drug-smuggling cases, including the June seizure of about 18 kg of hybrid ganja worth around Rs 18 crore from Perumbavoor and the October seizure of MDMA smuggled through Karipur airport in Malappuram. Searches were conducted at residences of accused persons including Abu Tahir, Harikrishnan, Jagath, and Jaisal in Kozhikode and Palakkad districts; a preliminary probe found they allegedly laundered large sums from trafficking hybrid ganja mainly smuggled from Thailand.

items.headline: Row over what was served for Sabarimala Onam feast
items.gist: Differences have emerged between Travancore Devaswom Board president K Jayakumar and Kerala Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan over Onam sadya served to devotees at Sabarimala, with Jayakumar initially denying reports that devotees got pulao while officials received sadya, and Muraleedharan claiming devotees were given pulao on Thiruvonam day. Jayakumar later acknowledged pulao was served at the Annadanam hall while sadya was organised in the staff mess, but said about 3,000 devotees who came for pulao were also served sadya.

items.headline: SC dismisses PIL challenging curbs on entry of journalists to schools
items.gist: The Supreme Court has dismissed a PIL by Priya Mishra challenging restrictions imposed by Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh education departments on entry of journalists, YouTubers, social-media personalities and civil-society members to government schools, including curbs on photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live-streaming. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said in its September 1 order that it was not inclined to entertain the Article 32 petition, including one challenging an August 16 Rajasthan circular requiring prior principal permission for outsiders.

items.headline: WIDESPREAD DAMAGE AFTER RAINS LASH UP'S THREE DISTRICTS; FIVE KILLED
items.gist: Five people, including three members of a family, were killed in separate rain-related incidents in Uttar Pradesh's Chitrakoot, Amethi and Barabanki districts, officials said on Thursday. A mud house collapse in Chitrakoot's Barachhi village killed Kallu Yadav (32) and two children; in Amethi, 66-year-old Shyamlal Chauhan died when a mud wall collapsed; and in Barabanki, 62-year-old Shalik Ram Kashyap died after a rain-weakened mud wall fell on him and his son-in-law, who survived.

items.headline: Tata Power commissions transmission corridor
items.gist: Tata Power on Thursday said it has commissioned the 400 kV Jalpura-Khurja transmission corridor in Uttar Pradesh, comprising a double-circuit transmission line from Khurja to Jalpura spanning 162 circuit kilometres and a gas-insulated switchgear substation at Jalpura with 1,000 MVA transformation capacity. Khurja is an important power node in Western Uttar Pradesh, playing a strategic role in enabling efficient transmission of power towards NCR and Noida.

items.headline: RPG Active Pharma acquires API biz
items.gist: RPG Life Sciences Ltd's wholly-owned subsidiary, RPG Active Pharma Ltd, has entered into a business transfer agreement to acquire the active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and intermediates business of Raghava Life Sciences for an amount up to Rs 135 crore. The transaction will be executed on a going-concern basis through a slump sale, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals, and includes a portfolio of 22 commercialised APIs and seven development-stage assets across therapeutic segments such as diabetes, cardiovascular and CNS.

items.headline: India-NZ trade likely by next month
items.gist: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement is likely to come into force next month on a mutually agreed date, an official said on Thursday, after the two countries signed the FTA on April 27 to boost two-way commerce in goods and services and promote investments. The pact provides duty-free access for 100 per cent of India's exports to New Zealand, which had maintained peak tariffs of up to 10 per cent on key Indian exports including ceramics, carpets, automobiles and auto components, and New Zealand has committed to invest USD 20 billion over 15 years.

items.headline: Inox Wind bags Rs 755-cr turnkey project
items.gist: Inox Wind on Thursday said it has secured a 100 MW wind energy turnkey order worth Rs 755 crore from Indian Oil Corporation, to be executed on a turnkey basis including post-commissioning operations and maintenance services. Under the order, Inox Wind will handle end-to-end project execution, including supply of wind turbine generators, engineering, procurement and construction, project execution, and post-commissioning O&M services.

items.headline: Prasol Chemicals fixes IPO price band
items.gist: Specialty chemicals manufacturer Prasol Chemicals Ltd is gearing up to launch its Rs 500-crore Initial Public Offering on September 8, with the price band fixed at Rs 643-676 per equity share; the IPO will close on September 10 and bidding for anchor investors will take place on September 7. The Rs 500-crore IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 80 crore and an Offer For Sale of shares worth up to Rs 420 crore by selling shareholders, with proceeds from the fresh issue to be used for payment of debt, working capital requirements and general corporate purposes.

items.headline: Adani Group bets big in non-BJP states
items.gist: The Adani Group is expanding its presence across Congress-led and other non-Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled states, pursuing or executing projects spanning roads, ports, power, renewable energy, cement and data centres totalling about Rs 5 lakh crore as state governments seek private capital for economic development, infrastructure and job creation. In Karnataka, Adani Enterprises emerged as the lowest bidder for both packages of the proposed 16.75-kilometre north-south tunnel road connecting Hebbal and Central Silk Board in Bengaluru at Rs 22,267 crore, Rs 3,500 crore lower than the second-lowest bidder; the group also has the 1,200-megawatt Udupi power plant and Mangaluru International Airport, with further investments across Kerala, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Bihar and Andhra Pradesh.

items.headline: 'Auto companies must prepare for end of EV subsidies'
items.gist: Government subsidies for electric vehicles will end in the coming years and companies need to be prepared for the challenge, Kamran Rizvi, Secretary in the Heavy Industries Ministry, said on Thursday while addressing the annual convention of the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers. He urged automobile and component makers to spend more on R&D, collaborate to set up charging infrastructure, and noted that electric three-wheelers account for 50 per cent of segment sales—well above the 10 per cent target for 2026—while two-wheelers are at 7 per cent electric penetration and cars at around 4-5 per cent, with demand for electric buses outstripping supply.

items.headline: Alliance Insurance settles over Rs 75 cr claims
items.gist: Alliance Insurance Brokers settled more than Rs 75 crore in insurance claims across jewellery and specie-related risks during the financial year ended March 2026, with employee dishonesty, theft and transit losses emerging as key areas of exposure. The broker settled Rs 32.26 crore in jewellery and specie insurance claims across 162 cases during FY2025-26 involving organised jewellery chains, wholesalers, exporters, manufacturers, retailers, bullion dealers, gold-for-loan businesses and individual customers, with employee or karigar dishonesty accounting for the largest share of claims by number and value.

items.headline: US trade pact to be ready when preferential rates are offered
items.gist: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday said the details of the Bilateral Trade Agreement with the US will be announced once Washington offers preferential terms compared to the country's competitors. He said India's nine free trade agreements spanning economies representing about USD 60 trillion of GDP would provide preferential access to nearly two-thirds of global trade, and that other FTAs with Canada, Mexico, Chile, Mercosur, SACU, GCC and Israel, together with efforts to review ASEAN, Korea and Japan deals, would give India access to 75 per cent of global trade at a rate lower than its competitors.

items.headline: Lumino shares debut at 34% premium
items.gist: Shares of Lumino Industries made a strong debut on bourses on Thursday, listing with a premium of more than 34 per cent against the issue price of Rs 82; the stock opened at Rs 110 on the NSE, a 34.15 per cent premium, and later jumped 44.15 per cent to Rs 118.20, while on the BSE it listed at Rs 109 and surged 45.11 per cent to Rs 118.99. The Rs 700-crore IPO in a price band of Rs 78-82 was subscribed 118.12 times on the final day of bidding on Monday, comprising a fresh issue worth up to Rs 500 crore and an Offer-for-Sale of up to Rs 200 crore by promoters Devendra Goel and Jay Goel.

items.headline: Supreme Court dismisses SEBI's plea against NSE
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Thursday disposed of pleas by the Securities and Exchange Board of India against the National Stock Exchange in the co-location and dark fibre cases after the market regulator approved around ₹1,500-crore settlement with the exchange. items.headline: Sebi mulls net settlement of cash market obligations for MFs
items.gist: Markets regulator Sebi on Thursday proposed permitting net settlement of funds for transactions undertaken by mutual fund schemes in the cash market, while continuing settlement of securities on a gross basis, aiming to reduce temporary liquidity requirements. The proposal is intended to facilitate ease of doing business, improve settlement efficiency and reduce temporary liquidity requirements for mutual fund schemes, while ensuring that existing safeguards relating to delivery-based settlement, scheme-wise accounting, valuation and investor protection remain unaffected, and comes after representations from market participants highlighting liquidity and operational inefficiencies during index rebalancing and large investor subscriptions or redemptions.

items.headline: India gets first Asian Games safeguarding officer in Neetal
items.gist: Following an Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) mandate, Neetal Narang will be India's first Safeguarding Officer at the Asian Games, serving as athletes' contact for harassment, abuse or neglect at the September 19–October 4 Aichi-Nagoya Games. President of the Softball Association of India and an internationally certified safeguarding officer, Narang will work with the OCA safeguarding officer to handle confidential complaints.

items.headline: Just 56 women in support staff
items.gist: India's 246-member Asian Games support staff includes only 56 women, about 22% of the total, prompting the Sports Ministry to direct the IOA to ensure adequate female doctors, physiotherapists and masseuses where squads lack them. Volleyball and E-Sports have no women support staff as only men compete, but the all-female three-member judo squad and golf's three women representatives also have no female support staff.

items.headline: Jamil defends dropping seniors, says picked India squad purely on merit
items.gist: Indian football head coach Khalid Jamil defended omitting established players from the 26-man squad for friendlies against Brazil, Uruguay and Panama, saying selections were merit-based after giving everyone an equal and adequate chance. Notable exclusions include former captain Sandesh Jhingan, Rahul Bheke, Lallianzuala Chhangte, Mohun Bagan goalkeeper Vishal Kaith, Durand Cup golden glove winner Liston Colaco and East Bengal midfielder Jeakson Singh.

items.headline: India, Belgium ink eight defence deals, boost military ties
items.gist: India and Belgium on Thursday signed eight contracts between arms companies and agreed to deploy senior defence officials in their respective embassies to promote industry cooperation, alongside a Letter of Intent for regular exchanges, staff talks and research cooperation. A Belgian frigate, Leopold, will visit India between November 5 and 8, Belgium conveyed it will not supply critical military hardware to Pakistan, and agreements cover ammunition, rockets, autonomous maritime systems, drones, counter-drones and armoured-vehicle systems.

items.headline: Kharge questions delay in FIR over 'purification' at Haldwani
items.gist: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday questioned the delay in filing an FIR for carrying out 'shudhikaran' at the site of his rally in Haldwani and asked Rajya Sabha Leader of the House JP Nadda to honour the promise he made in the Rajya Sabha to investigate the "act of untouchability". Kharge urged Nadda to direct Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Dhami to act on the incident that took place more than three weeks ago, and faulted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah for their "silence" on the issue.

The Ministry of Defence said the document provides a comprehensive framework aligning national security objectives with proactive global cooperation, with key pillars including strategic partnerships, capacity building, indigenous exports and maritime security.

items.headline: 31-member JPC set up to examine foreign funding bill
items.gist: A 31-member multi-party Joint Parliamentary Committee headed by BJP's Sanjay Jaiswal was constituted on Thursday to scrutinise the Foreign Contribution Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposes a designated authority to manage and dispose of assets if an organisation loses its FCRA licence. The panel has 21 MPs from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, with 19 NDA members and the rest from the Opposition, and has been asked to submit its report by the last day of the first week of the winter session.

items.headline: Centre tells SC it is examining CBSE three-language policy
items.gist: The Centre on Thursday informed the Supreme Court that it is examining suggestions for implementing the Central Board of Secondary Education's three-language policy, which requires Class 9 students to study three languages including two Indian languages. Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati submitted that the CBSE is finalising various modalities and sought time; the bench accepted the request and deferred the matter by a week.

items.headline: Fort St George preserves 400 yrs of history
items.gist: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced on Thursday that the Tamil Nadu government's Secretariat would be shifted out of Fort St George, the historic building that has served as the administrative centre since 1652 after land was bought in 1640. Spread over 107 acres, the heritage complex houses the Chief Minister's office, key departments including Home and Finance, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and a museum with over 3,661 antiquities; its six-metre-high walls withstood assaults including from Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan in the 18th century.

items.headline: 'Cracked his skull': Jantar Mantar claim sparks row
items.gist: A right-wing activist claiming credit in a video interview for the attack on a protester's father at Jantar Mantar during the students' agitation has triggered an uproar, with Rahul Gandhi on Thursday pledging support to the victim's daughter Nishu Azad and the Cockroach Janta Party announcing they will approach the police. Swatantra Bhardwaj was heard saying he "cracked the skull" of Nishu Azad's father Sanjay on June 23, that the injury needed 60 stitches and attracted Section 307, and that he was released after Delhi BJP leader Kapil Mishra's call.

items.headline: Nagaland urges Centre to roll back regulation for foreigners
items.gist: The Nagaland Assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the Centre to withdraw its Protected Area Permit system, which regulates the travel of foreign visitors to the frontier state. The resolution, moved by Deputy Chief Minister and BJP legislator Yanthungo Patton, stated that the PAP regime had hampered the growth of international tourism, investment, business engagement, cultural exchange and international partnerships.
items.paragraph: The Nagaland Assembly on Thursday unanimously passed a resolution urging the Centre to withdraw its Protected Area Permit system, which regulates the travel of foreign visitors to the frontier state. The House assured that appropriate systems for registration, regulation and monitoring of foreign nationals could be put in place through modern technology, noting that the Ministry of Home Affairs on December 17, 2024 reinforced the regime in Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram after earlier relaxations from January 1, 2011.

items.headline: Jagjivan calls for three-pronged strategy on food
items.gist: Union Agriculture Minister Jagjivan Ram, inaugurating a three-day Association of Food Scientists and Technologists symposium in Bangalore on "Strategies for storage, handling and processing of foodgrains in the present-day context," called on scientists and food technologists to evolve a three-pronged grain reserve strategy. items.headline: Why not have cameras, monitoring rooms at toll plazas, SC asks NHAI
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) why it cannot deploy camera surveillance systems and monitoring rooms at toll plazas to tackle rampant encroachment and stationary vehicles clogging national highways. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was hearing a suo motu case arising from a November 2, 2025 accident in Rajasthan’s Phalodi area that claimed 15 lives, and noted that encroachment and illegally parked vehicles were major contributors to road accidents.

items.headline: Gujarat man jailed in US for smuggling fentanyl chemicals
items.gist: A US court has sentenced Surat businessman Bhavesh Lathiya to 54 months — 4.5 years — in prison for distributing and smuggling fentanyl-precursor chemicals from India by mislabelling them as Vitamin C and using other “deceptive and fraudulent practices”. United States District Judge Pamela K Chen also ordered Lathiya, founder of Surat-based Raxuter Chemicals, to pay a forfeiture of $24,560 (a little more than Rs 23 lakh); he pleaded guilty in April and will be deported to India after completing his jail term.

The US Attorney’s Office said his firm sold and smuggled more than 50 pounds of chemicals used to manufacture fentanyl, a synthetic opioid said to be 100 times more powerful than morphine.

items.headline: Wife can't be expected to behave like Vodafone pug: HC
items.gist: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court set aside a trial court order refusing divorce to an estranged couple, observing that a wife cannot be expected to behave like the pug in the Vodafone advertisement and that it may not always be feasible for a husband to take his wife along whenever he is transferred. Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi granted divorce to a couple living apart for 16 years, directing the husband to pay Rs 7 lakh as alimony, and held that where a marriage has broken down irretrievably, continuing it would only mean giving sanction to cruelty.

items.headline: 160 detonators found near Secunderabad Army camp
items.gist: Three days after theft of service weapons and ammunition from the 20 Madras Regiment premises in Bollarum, Secunderabad Cantonment, 160 electric detonators were found near the Army camp on Wednesday, though police said they were unrelated to the arms theft and allegedly left behind during construction of a venture beside the golf course. Bollarum police registered a case against unidentified persons after a bomb disposal team identified the material as 33A-size commercial electric detonators packed in eight bundles in a plastic bucket near the firing range rear wall.

items.headline: TN to facilitate DNA tests of kin of those missing in Nepal floods
items.gist: The Tamil Nadu government said it would facilitate DNA tests of willing first-degree relatives of 85 people still missing after Nepal flash floods, of 305 pilgrims from the state who went to Kailash Mansarovar; 199 have returned on their own and 21 caught in the floods were rescued. Families can provide DNA samples at designated government laboratories in Chennai, Thanjavur and Madurai after the Nepal government requested samples from relatives of the missing.

items.headline: FLY91 inks firm order for 40 ATR aircraft
items.gist: Regional airline FLY91 signed a firm order for 40 ATR 72-600 aircraft valued at about $1 billion, the largest ATR order globally by any regional airline, and will lease another six to eight aircraft before deliveries begin. Unveiled in 2024 with 280 weekly flights to 12 destinations including Pune, Hubballi, Bengaluru, Goa, Kochi and Hyderabad, the airline marks ATR’s first big Indian order since IndiGo’s 50-aircraft deal in 2017.

items.headline: Services sector growth rises to 4-year high
items.gist: India’s services sector growth improved in August from an over four-year low in the previous month, supported by new orders that also helped job creation, according to an S&P Global industry survey released on Thursday. India’s services PMI rose to 54.1 in August from 53.3 in July, though the August figure was the second-weakest since March 2022 and remained below its long-run average of 54.5.

items.headline: India’s $136 billion haul aids rupee, but ups future risks
items.gist: The Indian rupee climbed to a two-month high on Thursday after a much larger-than-expected $136.4 billion raised through one-off measures improved the currency’s outlook at a time when renewed US-Iran conflict has pushed crude oil prices higher. The massive fundraising further swells the Reserve Bank of India’s already-record future dollar liabilities, potentially putting a ceiling on rupee appreciation; Nomura analysts estimate India’s balance of payments will be in a surplus of about $66 billion in the current fiscal year, against a deficit of $23.6 billion in the previous year.

items.headline: 32% of India’s workforce are frontier professionals: Report
items.gist: About 32% of India’s workforce are frontier professionals — people redesigning work around AI agents — double the global average of 16%, the Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026 showed. items.headline: Bharat NCAP 2.0 to be rolled out from October 2027, says Gadkari
items.gist: The Centre is planning to roll out a new version of the Bharat NCAP programme from October 2027, which will assess the complete safety framework and address the severe challenge of road accidents in the country, Union Minister Nitin Gadkari said on Thursday at the 66th SIAM Annual Convention 2026. He also announced a scheme for a rare emission control device for BS IV-compliant vehicles, costing Rs 4,000-5,000, with trials completed showing emissions after retrofitment on BS 4 vehicles same as BS 6.

items.headline: HC asks SIT to file final report by Sept. 25 in Sabarimala case
items.gist: The Kerala High Court directed the special investigation team probing alleged misappropriation of gold from the Sabarimala temple to submit its final report before the Vigilance Court, Kollam, on or before September 25. items.headline: A.P. Cabinet approves ₹4,054-cr. rural water works
items.gist: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved revival and rationalisation of 13,252 rural water supply works at an estimated cost of ₹4,053 crore, sanctioned a ₹950-crore government guarantee for an APTRANSCO loan from Power Finance Corporation, and approved ₹94 crore in price deficiency support for tobacco farmers. It also approved 78 flood-damage restoration works in Krishna, NTR, Guntur and Bapatla districts at a total cost of ₹624.88 lakh and several industrial land proposals.

items.headline: TTD ramps up medical facilities for nine-day Brahmotsavams
items.gist: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams is mounting a major medical preparedness drive for the nine-day Srivari Salakatla Brahmotsavams from September 15 to 23, deploying 75 additional doctors, 60 paramedics and 16 ambulances over and above the existing strength of 11 doctors and 139 paramedical staff. items.headline: Lawyers' case
items.gist: The Supreme Court on Thursday allowed young lawyers represented by advocate Prashant Bhushan, including Kunal Yadav, to approach the Delhi High Court for an independent investigation into alleged mob assault on August 21 while they were peacefully protesting at BCI premises for chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra’s resignation and regulatory reforms. Their petition said protesters were physically assaulted, dragged and forcibly thrown out inside CCTV-monitored BCI premises despite a large Delhi Police deployment including an Assistant Commissioner of Police who did not intervene.

items.headline: ED launches multi-State crackdown on narcotics networks across South
items.gist: The Enforcement Directorate on Thursday searched 30 locations across Tamil Nadu, Keralam, Karnataka and Telangana in eight narcotics-related cases under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act as part of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, probing money-laundering angles in NCB seizures including methamphetamine intercepts involving Sri Lankan nationals, Chennai hotel and Ambattur hauls, a Karnataka hashish and ganja case, Telangana properties linked to Kalapathi Nithu Bai, and Keralam cases involving hybrid ganja and MDMA from Muscat.

items.headline: SIR may be legal but is not fair: former Election Commissioner
items.gist: Former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa told the Professor Jagdeep Singh Chhokar Memorial Lecture organised by the Association for Democratic Reforms that statutory institutions are behaving as if “might is right,” citing the special intensive revision of electoral rolls as an unfair procedure validated by the judiciary despite deletion of 13 crore names. He said authorities may claim legality but fairness matters too, warned mass anxiety could disenchant voters when 33% already do not vote, and questioned whether parties seriously opposed measures such as electoral bonds.

items.headline: Govt. to spend ₹24,000 crore to modernise police force
items.gist: The Union government told the Supreme Court on Thursday it has begun implementing a ₹24,000-crore umbrella Police Modernisation Mission over five years to strengthen State police and Central Armed Police Forces through greater technology use. Additional Solicitor-General Rajkumar Bhaskar Thakare made the submission in a suo motu proceeding initiated in 2025 after media reports on non-functional CCTV cameras at Udaipur police stations, as the court reviewed compliance with its 2021 judgment mandating CCTV at key station locations including lock-ups and inspectors’ rooms.
